tasks.short: Prepare requirements documentation and issue the checked version.

steps.what: Collect the decisions the software developers still need.

loop.input: Meeting notes and mail that record decisions
loop.output: Rows for decision, owner and date
loop.check: The analyst drops a row that is still a question
loop.stop: One pass; a question is not stored as a decision
loop.why_not_simpler: Decisions sit in prose, so a fixed form misses them

steps.what: Draft the requirements documentation for the software developers.

loop.input: Decisions and the house requirements template
loop.output: Requirements with decision, scope and test
loop.check: The analyst deletes a requirement that cites no decision
loop.stop: Stop when every requirement has a decision or is removed
loop.why_not_simpler: The template needs prose tests, so a field list alone is not the document

steps.what: Check the requirements documentation against the agreed scope.
Issue the requirements documentation to the software developers.

tasks.design: Decisions are collected from notes, and {DOCS} drafts the requirements documentation in the house template. The analyst checks the draft against the agreed scope. Only that checked version is issued to the developers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements were rewritten from meeting memory, so a developer could not see which sentence was decided.
tasks.enabler_now: A template can hold decisions once they are written down. Vague decisions, and the scope check, cannot be skipped.
tasks.still_hard: A decision that was never actually made.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst knows which sentence is in scope and which the meeting left open.
tasks.altitude: Drafts start from decisions. The analyst still checks scope and can hold the issue. Decision rights on the requirements do not move.

reach.task: Say which operational rules the requirements must not contradict
reach.learn: Which developer requirements collide with an operational constraint

evidence.claim: Requirements that cite a recorded decision are a drafting task; an unmade decision is not.
Issuing requirements authorises a build, so the analyst checks the scope first.

assumptions: Focal role is the quantitative analyst. The developer's later coding is not this task. Boundary: from recorded decisions to issued requirements.
Structured fields are decision, owner, date, scope line and test. Meetings produce the decision; the analyst confirms scope. Fallback: a requirement with no decision is removed and is not issued.
Configure the house template in {DOCS} before custom code.
Upkeep of 5 hours per 100 baseline hours covers a new section in the template.
unknowns: Whether decisions are written down with an owner.
Whether the agreed scope is a document or a memory.
research_questions: What share of requirements cite a recorded decision?
How often is a draft line removed as out of scope?

incremental.description: Add a template section when a new requirement type appears

approvals.approved_version: requirements documentation the analyst checked against the agreed scope

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: decisions were not written down, so the draft is manual and the scope check is unchanged. High: decisions exist and only the draft shrinks. Vague items and the scope check stay.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Explain a carbon hedge to clients after judging the exposure.

steps.what: Extract the clients' carbon exposure from the positions.

loop.output: Rows for client, instrument, quantity and carbon factor
loop.check: The analyst checks a factor against the mandate source
loop.stop: One pass; a position with no factor stays blank
loop.why_not_simpler: Positions use different instrument names, so a fixed map misses factors

steps.what: Run hedge scenarios once the mandate fields exist.
Judge which hedge fits the carbon exposure and the mandate.
Explain the hedge to the clients and the limit of the advice.
Decide whether the clients put the hedge on.

tasks.design: The clients' carbon exposure is extracted, and {DATA_PLATFORM} runs hedge scenarios from the mandate fields. The analyst judges which hedge fits and explains it, including the limit of the advice. The clients decide whether to put the hedge on.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scenarios were rebuilt for each client, so the meeting was spent waiting on arithmetic.
tasks.enabler_now: Scenarios can run once exposure and mandate fields exist. Choosing the hedge, and explaining it, cannot.
tasks.still_hard: An exposure the mandate does not allow a hedge for.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst knows when a scenario fits the mandate and when it only fits the model.

ambition.what: A hedge is reviewed when the clients' exposure moves, not only at the annual meeting.

tasks.altitude: Scenarios are ready before the explanation. The analyst still judges the hedge and can refuse to recommend one. The clients keep the decision to transact.

reach.task: Say which carbon exposures look like an insurance risk
reach.learn: Which exposures an underwriter would not treat as hedgeable

evidence.claim: Choosing a hedge and explaining it to a client stay with the analyst.
A hedge proposal to a firm is outside annex III 5(b) credit scoring of natural persons; a sole trader as the client is the edge.

assumptions: Focal role is the quantitative analyst. The clients' decision to transact is not the analyst's saving. Boundary: from positions to an explanation. Executing the hedge is outside this task.

Structured fields are client, instrument, quantity, carbon factor and mandate limit. Positions produce quantity; the mandate produces the limit. Fallback: a position with no factor is left blank and is not hedged from a guess.
Configure the scenarios on {DATA_PLATFORM} before custom code.
Upkeep of 4 hours per 100 baseline hours covers a new factor on an instrument.
The client in view is a firm. A sole trader would need a separate review before any automated recommendation.
unknowns: Whether positions already carry a carbon factor.
Whether the client is a firm or a sole trader.
research_questions: What share of positions have a factor before the scenario?
How often is no hedge recommended?

incremental.description: Add a carbon factor for a new instrument

approvals.approved_version: hedge explanation the analyst gave against the checked scenarios and the mandate

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: factors are missing, so scenarios are not run and the explanation is prepared by hand. High: fields exist and only the scenarios shrink. The judgement and the explanation stay. The clients' decision is not saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Define green for funds and accept the assessment tool on known products.

steps.what: Define what green means for technologies and funds.
Map disclosed fields for green technologies and funds.

loop.output: Rows for product, field and value
loop.check: The analyst drops a field the definition does not use
loop.stop: One pass; a product with no matching field stays unmapped
loop.why_not_simpler: Disclosures name the same fact differently, so a fixed column list misses them

steps.what: Build the screen for green technologies from the mapped fields.
Try the tool on green financial products and investment funds.
Accept the green assessment tool or keep it off the library.

tasks.design: The analyst defines what green means for the technologies and funds in scope. Disclosed fields are mapped to that definition, and the screen is built from those fields. The tool is tried on products whose status is already known, and acceptance stays with the analyst.
tasks.previous_blocker: Screens used a vendor label as the definition, so a known product could pass for the wrong reason.
tasks.enabler_now: Mapping fields is feasible once the definition names them. Defining green, and accepting the tool, cannot.
tasks.still_hard: A product whose disclosure does not use the defined fields.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst knows when a passed trial still uses the wrong meaning of green.
tasks.altitude: Mapping follows the definition. The analyst still defines green and can keep the tool off the library. Decision rights on the definition do not move.

reach.task: Say which green claims an inspection will challenge
reach.learn: Which fund fields an inspector treats as evidence

evidence.claim: Defining what green means for a fund screen stays a judgement; a label is not a definition.
A screen can only test the fields the definition names.

assumptions: Focal role is the quantitative analyst. Boundary: from a definition to a library decision. Rating a live product for a client is later.

Structured fields are definition clause, field, product and known status. The analyst writes the definition; disclosures produce the field. Fallback: a product with no matching field is unmapped and is not marked green.
Configure the field map on {DATA_PLATFORM} before a custom screen.
Upkeep of 6 hours per 100 baseline hours covers a definition clause added to the map.
unknowns: Whether known products have an agreed green status.
Whether disclosures use stable field names.
research_questions: What share of products map to the definition?
How often does a trial pass for a reason the definition did not intend?

incremental.description: Add a definition clause to the field map

approvals.approved_version: acceptance of the green tool on the trial the analyst checked

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the definition is still unsettled, so mapping and the screen stay manual. High: fields are named and only the map shrinks. The definition, the build and the trial stay partly manual.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assess climate impact on damage, insurance costs and disruptions.

steps.what: Set the sites and perils for climate damage and business activities.
Load damage repairs, insurance costs and daily activity figures.

loop.input: Cost history for the sites and perils in scope
loop.output: Rows for site, peril, repair cost, insurance cost and activity
loop.check: The analyst checks a total against the source extract
loop.stop: One pass; a site with no history stays blank
loop.why_not_simpler: Costs sit in different ledgers, so one extract misses a peril

steps.what: Run the stored climate scenarios on the loaded figures.
Judge disruptions of daily activities the scenario misses.
File the climate impact note as the company record.

tasks.design: The analyst sets the sites and perils. Repair, insurance and activity figures are loaded, and stored climate scenarios run on those figures. Disruptions the scenario misses stay a judgement, and the impact note is filed only after the analyst checks it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scenarios were copied into a note, so a repair total could not be traced to a site.
tasks.enabler_now: Stored scenarios can run once sites and figures exist. Choosing the scope, and seeing a disruption the scenario omits, cannot.
tasks.still_hard: A peril or a site the stored scenarios do not contain.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst knows when a quiet scenario is missing a real disruption.

ambition.what: An impact note is refreshed when a site's repair history changes, not only once a year.

tasks.altitude: Scenarios are ready after the scope is set. The analyst still sets sites and perils and can hold the note. Decision rights on the scope do not move.

reach.task: Say which damage repairs a claim file already records
reach.learn: Which repair costs the scenario should not invent

evidence.claim: In a published spreadsheet-agent test, most models ended a cash waterfall at €1.16 million, not €580,000.
Judging a disruption a stored scenario does not show stays with the analyst.

assumptions: Focal role is the quantitative analyst. Boundary: from a scope choice to a filed impact note. Buying insurance is outside this task.

Structured fields are site, peril, repair cost, insurance cost and activity. The analyst sets the site; the ledgers produce the costs. Fallback: a site with no history is blank and is not given a zero loss.
Configure the scenario run on {DATA_PLATFORM} before custom code.
Upkeep of 5 hours per 100 baseline hours covers a peril added to the stored scenarios.
unknowns: Whether repair and insurance costs are stored by site.
Whether daily activity figures exist for those sites.
research_questions: What share of in-scope sites have a cost history?
How often does the analyst add a disruption the scenario missed?

incremental.description: Add a peril to the stored scenarios

approvals.approved_version: climate impact note the analyst checked against the scenario and the missed disruptions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: sites have no cost history, so scenarios are not run and the scope judgement is unchanged. High: figures load and only the scenario run shrinks. Scope and missed disruptions stay.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week is still checking scope, explaining hedges and defining what a screen means. Decisions, scenarios and mapped fields are ready beforehand. The analyst can hold a requirements issue, a hedge explanation or a tool.
reach: Logistics engineers: say which operational rules requirements must not contradict
Insurance underwriters: say which carbon exposures are not hedgeable
Claims adjusters, examiners, and investigators: say which damage repairs a claim file already records
skills_to_grow: Removing a requirement that cites no decision
Explaining the limit of a hedge before a client decides
Keeping a green tool off the library when the trial used the wrong meaning
role.ambitious_version: Every issued requirement cites a decision, every client hedge starts from a scenario the analyst will explain, and every climate note names the disruption the scenario missed.
